exclusions.name: Elena Cruz
exclusions.why_safe: She oversees receipts but does not control collection rate or shipping schedule, so her actions do not affect the number of units received.

exclusions.name: Other hospitals or blood centres
exclusions.why_safe: The question only concerns St. Vincent regional hospital's receipts from Cascade regional blood centre. No other sources or destinations are mentioned, and the evidence does not indicate any other transfers.

exclusions.name: Friday collection
exclusions.why_safe: The deadline is Friday noon, and the drive opens at 9:00 AM Friday. However, any units collected on Friday would not be shipped until the next scheduled shipment (Tuesday or Thursday), so they cannot be received by Friday noon. Thus excluding Friday collection is safe.

uncertainties.meaning: The actual number of usable units collected each day is unknown; the average rate of 12 units/hour may not hold exactly for each day, and the drive may be closed on Thursday (Friday is not included because deadline is Friday noon). Also, whether the centre's stock after collection on Thursday is sufficient for the Thursday shipment is uncertain.

It is unknown whether the centre's stock after Monday to Thursday collections (including the Tuesday shipment dispatch) will be at least 150 units by Thursday 4:00 PM. The initial stock is 40, collections add up to at most 12 units/hour * 8 hours/day * 4 days = 384 units, but the Tuesday shipment removes 150 units. So net stock before Thursday shipment could be 40 + 384 - 150 = 274, which is >150, but actual collections may vary.

It is uncertain whether the Thursday shipment will be dispatched and received by Friday noon. The shipment takes about 3 hours, so if dispatched at 4:00 PM Thursday, it arrives around 7:00 PM Thursday, well before Friday noon. However, if the centre does not have enough stock, the shipment may not occur.
